ExpressionCalculator.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initialize the instance with an empty postfix stack and a fixed operator priority table." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Create a new empty deque and assign it to self.postfix_stack. RESULT self.postfix_stack]
            [COMMAND Assign the fixed list of eight priority values [0, 3, 2, 1, -1, 1, 0, 2] to self.operat_priority. RESULT self.operat_priority]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ExpressionCalculator.calculate:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Evaluate a postfix expression by moving tokens from the postfix stack to a result stack, computing each operator with the top two values, and returning the final product-based evaluation as a float." MethodToTemplateConverter]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> expression </REF>: unknown "Expression to transform and evaluate."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: float "The final evaluated numeric result returned as a floating-point value."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Prepare internal state using the transformed input expression. RESULT prepared_state]
            [COMMAND Initialize an empty result stack as a deque. RESULT result_stack]
            [COMMAND Reverse the postfix token stack so tokens can be consumed in evaluation order. RESULT self.postfix_stack]
            [COMMAND While the postfix stack is not empty, pop the next token and process it. RESULT current_op]
            [COMMAND Within the while loop, if the popped token is not an operator, replace every '~' with '-' and append the normalized token to the result stack. RESULT result_stack]
            [COMMAND Within the while loop, if the popped token is an operator, pop the second value and then the first value from the result stack. RESULT first_value, second_value]
            [COMMAND Within the operator branch, normalize both popped values by replacing every '~' with '-'. RESULT first_value, second_value]
            [COMMAND Within the operator branch, compute the intermediate result by calling _calculate with the normalized first value, normalized second value, and the operator. RESULT temp_result]
            [COMMAND Within the operator branch, convert the intermediate result to a string and append it to the result stack. RESULT result_stack]
            [COMMAND After all postfix tokens have been processed, join the remaining result stack items with '*' and evaluate the expression, then return the numeric value as a float. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ExpressionCalculator.prepare:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Parse the input expression into postfix form by scanning characters, buffering operand substrings, and using an operator stack to handle precedence and parentheses." prepare]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> expression </REF>: string "Input expression to be converted into postfix form."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: none "The method does not return a value; it appends tokens to the internal postfix stack."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize the operator stack with a default delimiter token ',' and convert the input expression into a character array, then set the current segment start index and character count to 0. RESULT op_stack, arr, current_index, count]
            [COMMAND Within the outer loop over each character index i and token current_op in the character array, check whether the current token is an operator. RESULT current_op classification]
            [COMMAND Within the operator branch, if count is greater than 0, append the buffered substring from current_index to current_index + count to the postfix stack. RESULT postfix_stack]
            [COMMAND Within the operator branch, read the top of the operator stack into peek_op. RESULT peek_op]
            [COMMAND Within the operator branch, if current_op is ')', repeatedly pop operators from op_stack and append them to the postfix stack until '(' is on top, then pop the '(' marker. RESULT postfix_stack, op_stack]
            [COMMAND Within the operator branch, if current_op is not ')', repeatedly pop operators from op_stack and append them to the postfix stack while current_op is not '(' and peek_op is not ',' and compare(current_op, peek_op) is true; after each pop, refresh peek_op from the new stack top, then push current_op onto op_stack. RESULT postfix_stack, op_stack]
            [COMMAND Within the operator branch after handling the current operator, reset count to 0 and advance current_index to i + 1. RESULT count, current_index]
            [COMMAND Within the non-operator branch, increment count to extend the current buffered operand segment. RESULT count]
            [COMMAND After the loop, if count is greater than 1 or count is exactly 1 and the token at arr[current_index] is not an operator, append the final buffered substring from current_index to current_index + count to the postfix stack. RESULT postfix_stack]
            [COMMAND After all characters are processed, pop and append remaining operators from op_stack until the default delimiter ',' is reached. RESULT postfix_stack, op_stack]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ExpressionCalculator.is_operator:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Returns whether the input character is one of the predefined operator-like symbols in the fixed set." is_operator]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> c </REF>: character "The character to test for membership in the operator symbol set."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: boolean "True when the input character is one of +, -, *, /, (, ), or %, otherwise false."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether the input character c is a member of the fixed set {'+', '-', '*', '/', '(', ')', '%'}. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ExpressionCalculator.compare:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Normalize percent signs to forward slashes in both inputs, then return whether the operator priority of peek is greater than or equal to the operator priority of cur." compare]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Instance that provides the operator priority table."
        <REF> cur </REF>: character "Current operator character to normalize and compare."
        <REF> peek </REF>: character "Next operator character to normalize and compare."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: boolean "True if the priority of peek is at least the priority of cur after normalization; otherwise false."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND If cur is '%', reassign cur to '/' before any priority lookup. RESULT cur]
            [COMMAND If peek is '%', reassign peek to '/' before any priority lookup. RESULT peek]
            [COMMAND Look up the priority values for peek and cur using ord(character) - 40 as the index into self.operat_priority, then compare the two priorities with >=. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ExpressionCalculator._calculate:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Dispatch on the operator string to perform the corresponding Decimal arithmetic on two values, or raise an error for an unsupported operator." _calculate]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> first_value </REF>: number or string convertible to Decimal "The left operand to convert to Decimal before arithmetic."
        <REF> second_value </REF>: number or string convertible to Decimal "The right operand to convert to Decimal before arithmetic."
        <REF> current_op </REF>: string "The arithmetic operator to apply: '+', '-', '*', '/', or '%'."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: Decimal "The Decimal result of the selected arithmetic operation."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Compare current_op to '+'. RESULT branch_check_1]
            [COMMAND If current_op equals '+', convert first_value and second_value to Decimal and return their sum immediately. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Otherwise compare current_op to '-' and continue through the operator checks in order. RESULT branch_check_2]
            [COMMAND If current_op equals '-', convert first_value and second_value to Decimal and return their difference immediately. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Otherwise compare current_op to '*' and continue through the operator checks in order. RESULT branch_check_3]
            [COMMAND If current_op equals '*', convert first_value and second_value to Decimal and return their product immediately. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Otherwise compare current_op to '/' and continue through the operator checks in order. RESULT branch_check_4]
            [COMMAND If current_op equals '/', convert first_value and second_value to Decimal and return their quotient immediately. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Otherwise compare current_op to '%' and continue through the operator checks in order. RESULT branch_check_5]
            [COMMAND If current_op equals '%', convert first_value and second_value to Decimal and return their remainder immediately. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: current_op is not '+', '-', '*', '/', or '%'.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Raise a ValueError identifying current_op as an unexpected operator. RESULT error]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: current_op does not match any supported operator branch.]
        [LOG "Unexpected operator: current_op is rejected after all supported arithmetic checks fail."]
        [THROW ValueError "Indicates that the operator is not one of the supported arithmetic symbols."]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ExpressionCalculator.transform:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Normalize an expression by removing whitespace and a trailing equals sign, convert the string to a character list, replace unary minus signs with tildes during a scan, and handle a leading negative parenthesized expression as a special case by restoring the minus sign and prepending 0." transform]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> expression </REF>: string "Arithmetic-like expression string to normalize and transform."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "Transformed expression string after unary minus handling and optional leading zero insertion."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Remove all whitespace characters from the input expression. RESULT expression]
            [COMMAND Remove a trailing equals sign only if it appears at the very end of the expression. RESULT expression]
            [COMMAND Convert the cleaned expression string into a list of individual characters. RESULT arr]
            [COMMAND Within the scan over arr from left to right, inspect each character and look for minus signs. RESULT i_and_c]
            [COMMAND Within the scan over arr, when the current character is a minus sign at index 0, replace that minus sign with a tilde. RESULT arr]
            [COMMAND Within the scan over arr, when the current character is a minus sign at a nonzero index, read the previous character from arr[i - 1]. RESULT prev_c]
            [COMMAND Within the scan over arr, when the previous character is one of +, -, *, /, (, E, or e, replace the current minus sign with a tilde to mark it as unary minus. RESULT arr]
            [COMMAND After the scan, if the first character is a tilde and the second character exists and is an opening parenthesis, restore the first character to a minus sign and return the joined array prefixed with 0. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Otherwise, return the joined character array without any prefix. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
